answer: Run every new identity through a privacy-preserving set intersection: each applicant commits an encrypted hash of one real-world credential, and a multi-party computation compares the whole grove of commitments without revealing whose is whose. Like a prism splitting one beam into distinct colours, duplicates split out as identical hashes and are refused before any reward. A farmer must buy a fresh umber-stamped credential for every fake, while an honest agent passes once. Limit: it trusts the issuers, and a small set leaks membership by elimination.
